During the Second Boer War, Britain’s scorched-earth campaign forced tens of thousands of Boer and Black South African civilians into concentration camps. Disease, hunger, overcrowding, and poor sanitation turned these camps into a humanitarian catastrophe, killing tens of thousands, many of them children and leaving a dark legacy of the British Empire.
